Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Infected leaves turn yellow and drop early. Fruit develops dark, scabby, cracked lesions and becomes deformed.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant scab-resistant apple varieties. Prune trees for good air circulation. Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to remove the fungus. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Apply protectant fungicides (captan or mancozeb) from bud break, repeating every 7-10 days during wet spring weather. Remove and burn severely infected leaves and fruit.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular purple-bordered 'frog-eye' leaf spots. Fruit shows firm, dark, concentric brown rot. Cankers with cracked bark appear on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out dead wood and cankered branches, which harbour the fungus. Remove mummified fruit from trees. Keep trees healthy and avoid wounding.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Apply captan or thiophanate-methyl fungicides from petal fall. Cut away cankers well below the infection and destroy all pruned material away from the orchard.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces, later forming tube-like structures underneath. Fruit may show distorted orange lesions.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Do not plant apples near juniper or red cedar trees, the alternate host. Choose rust-resistant cultivars. Remove nearby cedar galls before spring.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb fungicide from pink bud stage through early summer, targeting the spore-release period after rain.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are uniformly green with normal shape and no spots or lesions.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced fertilisation, regular pruning and good orchard sanitation to keep trees healthy.
Apple___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring and preventive care.

Background___Background.symptoms: The image does not appear to contain a clear crop leaf.
Background___Background.prevention: Capture a single leaf filling most of the frame, on a plain background, in good daylight.
Background___Background.management: Please retake the photo of the affected leaf and try again.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Foliage is healthy and green.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5), mulch well and ensure good drainage.
Blueberry___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care and monitoring.

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves and shoots. Young leaves may curl, twist and become stunted. Fruit can develop a whitish coating.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune to open the canopy for airflow and sunlight. Avoid excess nitrogen that promotes soft new growth. Remove infected shoots.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.management: Apply sulfur or potassium-bicarbonate sprays at first signs. Myclobutanil fungicide is effective; repeat at label intervals during dry, warm spells.

Cherry___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are green and undamaged.
Cherry___healthy.prevention: Prune annually, keep the base weed-free and monitor for pests.
Cherry___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care.

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular grey-to-tan lesions running parallel to the leaf veins. Lesions merge in severe cases, blighting whole leaves and reducing grain fill.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.prevention: Rotate crops away from maize for at least one season. Plough under or remove crop residue. Grow resistant hybrids and avoid dense planting.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.management: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides at early tasseling if disease is spreading. Improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces, later turning brownish-black. Heavy infection yellows and dries the leaves.
Corn___Common_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids and sow early to avoid peak humid conditions. Avoid excessive nitrogen.
Corn___Common_rust.management: Fungicides (mancozeb or triazoles) help when applied early in susceptible fields. Usually resistant hybrids make sprays unnecessary.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on the leaves. Lesions enlarge and coalesce, giving a scorched, burnt appearance from the lower leaves upward.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops and bury infected residue by tillage. Avoid continuous maize cropping.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Apply foliar fungicide (azoxystrobin or propiconazole) from early lesion stage through tasseling if weather stays wet.

Corn___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are green and upright.
Corn___healthy.prevention: Follow balanced fertilisation and crop rotation. Scout fields weekly.
Corn___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan circular leaf spots with dark borders. Berries develop brown soft spots, then shrivel into hard black mummies on the bunch.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected tendrils during pruning. Train vines for airflow. Avoid dense canopies.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Apply mancozeb or myclobutanil from early shoot growth through fruit set, especially during warm wet weather.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellow or red bands between leaf veins. Dark spots on berries ('measles'). Sudden vine collapse can occur in hot weather.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid large pruning wounds and protect them when made. Remove and destroy dead wood and severely affected vines.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: No reliable chemical cure exists. Manage by cutting out infected wood, maintaining vine vigour and protecting pruning cuts with sealant.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown angular spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo. Heavy spotting causes leaves to dry and fall early.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve canopy airflow by pruning. Remove fallen leaves. Avoid overhead watering.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Apply copper-based or mancozeb fungicides at first symptoms and repeat during the rainy season.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Foliage is green and intact.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Prune for airflow, manage canopy and monitor regularly.
Grape___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellowing (mottling) of leaves. Lopsided, small, bitter green fruit. Overall tree decline and twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free saplings. Control the Asian citrus psyllid insect that spreads the bacterium. Remove and destroy infected trees promptly.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: No cure is available. Control psyllid vectors with insecticides, remove infected trees, and maintain tree nutrition to prolong productivity.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark angular spots on leaves that drop out to give a 'shot-hole' look. Fruit shows dark pitted cracked spots. Heavy leaf drop weakens the tree.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid high-nitrogen fertiliser. Ensure good air movement and avoid overhead irrigation.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Apply copper sprays at dormancy and oxytetracycline during the season where permitted. Reduce tree stress with proper watering and nutrition.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are healthy and green.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Prune annually, thin fruit and keep the orchard clean.
Peach___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care.

Pepper___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halos. Leaves drop; fruit develops raised scabby spots. Spreads fast in warm wet weather.
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified clean seed and resistant varieties. Rotate crops, avoid working plants when wet, and do not use overhead irrigation.
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.management: Apply copper-mancozeb sprays preventively. Remove badly infected plants and avoid handling healthy plants afterwards.

Pepper___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Plant foliage is green and vigorous.
Pepper___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, mulch and maintain even moisture.
Pepper___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ('target spots') on older lower leaves, surrounded by yellowing. Severe cases defoliate the plant and shrink tubers.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate with non-host crops. Use certified seed tubers. Keep plants well-nourished and avoid water stress. Remove volunteer plants and debris.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms and repeat every 7-10 days. Hill soil over tubers and avoid late-evening irrigation.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large dark water-soaked blotches on leaves with pale green margins, and white fungal growth underneath in humid weather. Rapidly rots foliage and tubers. This is the disease behind historic famines.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and certified seed. Destroy cull piles and volunteers. Ensure good drainage and airflow. Act fast in cool wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Apply protectant fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) before infection and systemic ones (cymoxanil, metalaxyl) once detected. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Foliage is green and healthy.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops and hill plants properly.
Potato___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Canes and leaves look healthy.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Thin canes for airflow, mulch and remove old fruited canes.
Raspberry___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are uniformly green.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, use good seed and scout for pests regularly.
Soybean___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems that spread to cover the surface. Leaves yellow, curl and die early, reducing yield and fruit quality.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Grow resistant varieties, space plants well and plant in full sun. Avoid excess nitrogen and overhead watering.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Spray sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or neem oil at first spotting. Repeat weekly. Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small dark purple spots on leaves that enlarge and merge, giving a scorched, reddish-brown look. Heavy infection weakens plants and lowers yield.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Use disease-free runners and resistant varieties. Space plants for airflow, renovate beds after harvest, and remove old infected leaves.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Apply captan or myclobutanil fungicides from early growth. Improve drainage and avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Leaves are green and healthy.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Renovate beds, mulch with straw and keep foliage dry.
Strawberry___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine care.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves with yellow halos; leaves may tear and drop. Fruit develops raised scabby brown spots. Spreads rapidly in warm wet conditions.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified clean seed and resistant varieties. Rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, and do not work among wet plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Apply copper-based sprays (often with mancozeb) preventively. Remove infected plants and debris; disinfect tools.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown target-like spots with concentric rings on lower, older leaves, surrounded by yellowing. Stem and fruit lesions may form. Causes progressive defoliation.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants, mulch to stop soil splash, and space for airflow. Remove lower infected leaves early.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days once spots appear. Keep plants well fed and watered at the base.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green blotches on leaves and stems with white mould underneath in humid weather. Fruit shows firm brown greasy rot. Can destroy a crop within days.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and clean transplants. Ensure airflow and drainage. Scout closely during cool, wet, humid spells.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Act immediately: apply protectant fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) and systemic ones (cymoxanil) when detected. Remove and destroy infected plants off-site.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with olive-green to grey velvety mould underneath. Common in humid greenhouses; leaves yellow and drop.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Lower humidity by ventilation and wider spacing. Avoid wetting leaves. Use resistant varieties in protected cultivation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Improve air circulation and reduce humidity first. Apply chlorothalonil or copper fungicides; remove affected leaves.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark borders and grey centres on lower leaves, each with tiny black specks. Heavy spotting yellows and drops leaves from the bottom up.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops, mulch to block soil splash, stake plants and remove lower infected leaves. Avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms and repeat every 7-10 days in wet weather. Clear all crop debris after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or speckling on leaves, with fine webbing underneath in heavy infestations. Leaves bronze, dry and fall. Worst in hot, dry weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid water stress and dusty conditions. Encourage natural predators. Hose down foliage periodically in hot spells.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.management: Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil or a miticide, covering leaf undersides. Repeat to catch new generations. Remove severely infested leaves.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small brown spots that enlarge into target-like lesions with concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit. Severe infection causes leaf drop and fruit blemishes.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops, improve airflow with staking and spacing, and avoid overhead irrigation. Remove crop residue.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb or azoxystrobin at first symptoms and repeat during humid weather.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins, severe stunting, and bushy growth with few or no fruit. Spread by whiteflies.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties and virus-free transplants. Control whiteflies with insect nets, reflective mulch and insecticides. Remove infected plants early.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: No cure once infected. Remove and destroy infected plants to limit spread and focus on whitefly control for the rest of the crop.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, with curling, puckering and stunted growth. Fruit may be distorted with uneven ripening.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use certified virus-free seed and resistant varieties. Wash hands and tools; avoid tobacco contact. Remove and destroy infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: No chemical cure. Remove infected plants, disinfect tools and hands, and control weeds that host the virus.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Plant foliage is green and vigorous.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, stake and mulch plants, and water at the base.
Tomato___healthy.management: No treatment required. Continue routine monitoring.
